title: Active Job & Action Mailer — Quick Revision

sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Active Job is Rails' queue adapter abstraction — define your job once, switch the backend from Sidekiq to GoodJob to inline (for tests) without changing application code. The interview questions probe the adapter trade-offs: Sidekiq is fastest but requires Redis; GoodJob uses PostgreSQL so no extra infrastructure; inline is for tests. Action Mailer builds on top of Active Job via deliver_later — the email is queued rather than sent synchronously. This page covers Active Job callbacks, queue name conventions, job inheritance, Action Mailer delivery methods (SMTP, SendGrid, SES), mailer previews in development, parameterised mailers, and testing both — asserting that an email was enqueued (not just that the mail object was created).

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: active-job-patterns, action-mailer, delivery-methods. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
